name: SLOJ PO SLOJ (Layer by Layer): a cinematic 3D roof assembly
oneLiner: A real-time 3D Zagreb house whose anthracite roof builds itself layer by layer as you scroll (rafters, membrane, battens, sheets, flashings, chimney, snow guards, gutters, then a rain test), lit like an Apple product shot, ending in a match-cut to a real Karamatić roof with the line 'Ovo nije render.'

heroStoryboard.beat: The screen is #0B0D0F. The pre-rendered poster of the finished house is already painted as the LCP image, at a 3/4 low angle on a dark studio background. A 1px #D7141A hairline draws left to right along the poster's eave line. It also works as the 3D loader: its scaleX follows drei useProgress, with a 0.6 s minimum.

The red hairline lifts at the centre into a Λ, the red A-peak from the KARAMATIĆ logo, and locks onto the house's ridge. The WebGL canvas crossfades in over the poster with pixel-identical framing, so nothing pops. A softbox Lightformer sweeps left to right across the anthracite sheets in 1.2 s (power2.inOut) and drags a long specular streak. Idle state: the camera breathes ±0.6° yaw on an 8 s sine.

The H1 'Od letve do sljemena.' (Archivo wdth 125 / wght 850) reveals word by word from under a mask (SplitText, y 105% to 0, stagger 0.08, expo.out). Then the subline 'Limeni krovovi, opšavi, dimnjaci i oluci. Zagreb i okolica.', two CTAs ([Besplatna procjena] red, [Nazovi 09x xxx xxxx] outline) and a trust row (Google rating, number of roofs, years). At the bottom: 'Pomakni dolje i složit ćemo krov pred vama', with a red chevron that drops like a sheet.

The pin starts. The headline and CTAs translate up and out, and the CTA morphs (FLIP) into the sticky-header button. The camera rises from 12° to 30° elevation, orbits +20° azimuth, fov 35 to 32. The roof explodes along the roof normal into hovering layers: membrane +0.6 m, battens +1.2 m, sheets +2.0 m, flashings +2.6 m, snow guards +3.0 m. Gutters slide 0.8 m out horizontally, the chimney cladding splits into 4 sheets and the barrel cap rises 1.5 m. power3.inOut, 60 ms stagger, top layer first.

Eight mono labels with SVG leader lines draw in, one per layer: 01 Konstrukcija, 02 Folija, 03 Letve, 04 Pokrov, 05 Opšavi, 06 Dimnjak, 07 Snjegobrani, 08 Oluci. The whole stack keeps turning slowly (6°) so the hold stays alive. Side copy: 'Krov nije jedan sloj. Ovo je osam razloga zašto naš ne prokišnjava.'

Every layer except the structure fades to a ghost: 8% opacity plus drei <Edges> in #8A939B, so the viewer sees what is coming. The camera eases down to a rafter-level 3/4 view. The step counter '01 / 08' appears at the left and works as a jump link.

A red scan line travels up the rafters from eave to ridge as an inspection. One rafter flashes red and is swapped from old brown to fresh pine #C9A273, with the copy 'Truli rog ne pokrivamo, mijenjamo ga.' The vapour-permeable membrane then unrolls in strips from the eave upward: a clip-plane reveal along the slope, plus a vertex-sine cloth wobble that damps to 0 and visible overlap seams. Copy: 'Krov diše, voda ne prolazi.'

Counter-battens drop along each rafter (25 ms stagger). Horizontal battens then cascade bottom to top at the sheet module, with a mono callout 'razmak 350 mm'. Gutter hooks (kuke) clip onto the eave board. Showing them before the roofing is a deliberate craft-accuracy nod.

The camera goes low along the eave and looks up the slope. Ghost sheets turn solid and drop column by column from the left gable. Per-instance delays live in the vertex shader. Each sheet falls 40 cm (power3.in), settles with a 1.5 cm overshoot and catches a white specular glint on impact. On 3 hero impacts there is a 0.15° camera shake, and Android gets a 6 ms navigator.vibrate tick on every 4th sheet. Then 600 screw heads pop in as a ripple from eave to ridge (scale 0 to 1, 2 ms stagger). The camera pulls back to show both planes covered. Copy: 'Crijep-lim, falc ili trapez. Antracit RAL 7016 ili boja po želji.'

A red cut line first traces the ridge, the valley and both verges, and the metal follows it. The ridge cap extrudes end to end (scale.x 0 to 1), the valley flashing slides down the valley, and the verge trims fold 90° over the gable edge on their hinges. The camera dollies along the ridge. Copy: 'Tu krovovi najčešće procure. Zato tu radimo najsporije.'

Close-up on the chimney, fov 28. Four anthracite sheets fold around the brick chimney like origami (90° hinge rotations, 120 ms stagger) and the step flashing tucks under the sheets. The barrel cap comes down on its 4 legs and settles. Real photo 8 then slides in beside it as a portrait card with a 35° pitch-wipe: 'Isti detalj. Pravi krov, Zagreb.'

The camera rises to a drone-like, almost top-down view that mirrors photos 5 and 13. Rows of triangular snow guards pop in row by row (back.out 1.4). About 300 snow sprites slide down the steel and stop against the guards. Copy: 'Snijeg ostaje na krovu, a ne na autu ispod.'

The half-round gutter reveals along the eave from left to right (clip plane). The downpipe extrudes down to the ground and bends into the drain. RAIN TEST: about 1,500 instanced streaks fall. The steel turns wet (roughness 0.38 to 0.12, with a scrolling streak normal), water threads run into the gutter and pour out of the downpipe. A badge reads 'Testirano kišom.'

The rain stops. The procedural environment lerps from cool studio to golden hour: key Lightformer #F2A65A, backdrop gradient #1B2430 to #F2A65A. A long shadow sweeps across the roof, and the camera returns to a higher 3/4 framing whose ridge diagonal matches photo 17.

A 35° pitch-wipe running along the ridge line replaces the render with real photo 17, full-bleed in the same golden light. Large text: 'Ovo nije render.' Small text: 'Krov u Zagrebu. Napravila ekipa Karamatić.' The pin releases into the stats/projects section. A 'Preskoči animaciju' link stays visible in the corner for the whole pin.

heroMobileFallback: The device tier is decided before any 3D byte loads. Signals: navigator.connection.saveData and effectiveType, deviceMemory, WebGL2 support, GPU renderer string via detect-gpu (with self-hosted benchmark JSON), and prefers-reduced-motion. TIER B, modern phones (iPhone 12+, Galaxy A54/S21-class): the same scene in 'lite' mode. It uses a portrait camera path that is higher and more drone-like (it mirrors photos 5 and 13), shortens the pin to 380svh and clamps DPR to 1.5. It drops post-processing and camera shake, has no haptics on iOS, and swaps the rain for an animated water line along the gutter. Snow is cut to 80 sprites and the crijep-lim steps become a normal map. Labels move to a bottom sheet with a '04 / 08' counter instead of leader lines. Lenis is off (native touch scroll) and ScrollTrigger uses ignoreMobileResize with svh units. drei PerformanceMonitor steps quality down, and if FPS stays under 30 for 3 s it hot-swaps to Tier C at the same beat. TIER C (low-end Android/Mali, Save-Data, 2G/3G, reduced motion, no WebGL2, context loss, or 3D not ready within 4 s): zero WebGL. The hero is the pre-rendered portrait poster (AVIF ~70 KB) with identical HTML headline and CTAs. Below it, a 'Sloj po sloj' horizontal snap carousel shows 8 pre-rendered stills (AVIF 35-45 KB each, lazy-loaded) with the same captions, a CSS crossfade and a 4% Ken Burns per step. The configurator becomes swatches over 15 pre-rendered images that load on tap. The stills come from the live scene via a Playwright '?still=' route, so all tiers look like one product. A Phase-1 launch can ship Tier C to everyone and switch 3D on later without changing the layout.
heroTech: Astro page with exactly one React island: three.js + React Three Fiber + drei, driven by a single GSAP ScrollTrigger master timeline (scrub 0.8) over a pinned section, with Lenis smooth scroll on desktop only. The scene is split in two to solve sourcing and file size. (1) Static parts are modelled in Blender: the house shell (10x8 m Zagreb-suburb house, attic, 35° gable roof plus a cross-gable so a real valley exists), the brick chimney and the barrel chimney cap. AO is baked to vertex colours, so no texture is needed, and the export goes through glTF-Transform CLI (meshopt, quantize, prune, webp) to stay at or under 250 KB. (2) Every animatable roof layer is generated in code, so it costs nothing to download and the profile switcher only has to swap one sheet geometry (crijep-lim / falcani lim / trapez). InstancedMesh covers rafters, counter-battens, battens, gutter hooks, sheets, screws and snow guards. ExtrudeGeometry along roof edges builds the ridge, valley and verge flashings, and TubeGeometry builds the gutter and downpipe. All per-instance motion (drop, settle, fold, pop) runs in the vertex shader via three-custom-shader-material on MeshPhysicalMaterial. Each instance carries aDelay/aAxis attributes and each layer has one uProgress uniform. GSAP tweens about 20 numbers in a ref, with no per-frame React state. Lighting uses no HDR file: a drei <Environment> is built from 3-4 <Lightformer> softbox strips (animated for the light sweep, lerped to golden hour at the end), with AgX/ACES tone mapping and a one-frame baked AccumulativeShadows. Materials: steel MeshPhysical #383E42 (metalness 0.55, roughness 0.38, clearcoat 0.25); walls matte #ECEBE6 like an architect's maquette, which echoes the logo's white house; timber #C9A273. Labels are a DOM overlay positioned by projecting 8 anchor points per frame, so they are crisp, real, indexable HTML. One canvas serves the whole page through drei <View>: the hero, the services mini-roof and the configurator share one WebGL context. Post-processing is desktop only: SMAA, faint bloom on red highlights, vignette. Camera choreography is a set of {pos, target, fov} keyframes on a CatmullRom path, tuned with a dev-only leva 'log camera' panel. The poster and fallback stills are rendered from the same scene by Playwright and encoded with sharp, so the poster-to-canvas swap is pixel-identical. References: Apple's exploded product views, Rivian's configurator colour swaps, and Igloo Inc's scroll-driven 3D.

homepageSections.content: 6-8 real questions: duration, whether old tiles must come off, rain/winter work, warranty, rough price drivers, permits, noise of a metal roof.

homepageSections.content: A 3-step form. 1: what is needed (chips: novi krov, popravak, opšavi/atika, dimnjak, oluci, drugo). 2: location plus up to 6 roof photos uploaded from the phone. 3: name, phone, when to call. Big alternatives beside it: Nazovi / WhatsApp / Viber. Footer: company data (OIB, address), working hours, privacy policy.

typography: Display: Archivo (Google Fonts, variable, wdth 62-125 and wght 100-900, includes latin-ext). Headlines are set at wdth 125, wght 800-900, sentence case, tracking -0.02em, leading 0.95, fluid H1 clamp(2.75rem, 7vw + 1rem, 7.5rem). The wide, heavy cut matches the logo's 'KARAMATIĆ', so the logo redraw can be built from Archivo itself plus the red Λ, unifying brand and site. Body/UI: Inter (variable, latin-ext), 16-18px, leading 1.55. Technical labels: JetBrains Mono (latin-ext) for layer labels, the '04 / 08' counters, dimensions ('razmak 350 mm'), RAL codes and the counters' odometer digits. This mono layer is what makes the page read 'engineered' rather than 'brochure'. Load: self-host via Fontsource (@fontsource-variable/archivo with the wdth+wght file, @fontsource-variable/inter, @fontsource/jetbrains-mono). Always load the latin AND latin-ext subsets, or subset one file with pyftsubset covering U+0000-00FF plus U+0106-0107 (Ćć), U+010C-010D (Čč), U+0110-0111 (Đđ), U+0160-0161 (Šš), U+017D-017E (Žž). Preload only the two above-the-fold woff2 files, use font-display swap with size-adjusted fallbacks to avoid CLS, and test 'Ć' and 'Đ' at wdth 125 / wght 900 before sign-off.
texturesAndMotion: The material language is the client's actual product: anthracite coated steel against a black studio, with one red line. The 3D look is 'architect's maquette meets product shot': a matte off-white house, physically based anthracite steel with a soft clearcoat, pine timber, and no attempt at photoreal grass, trees or sky (that looks cheap and is heavy). The 3-4 procedural softbox strips mean every camera move drags a long specular streak across the sheets, and that streak is where the premium feeling comes from. UI textures: (1) a 'falc' seam pattern, vertical lines every 48px at 4% white on dark sections (CSS repeating-linear-gradient); (2) static 3% film grain (a 128px tiled PNG) over both photos and renders, so phone photos and CG live in one world; (3) 1px #383E42 hairlines. No brushed-metal gradients, bevels or glassmorphism, even though the logo has them. Motion rules: metal has mass. Heavy things fall (power3.in) and settle with at most 2% overshoot, and nothing is springy. UI enters with expo.out over 0.7-0.9 s. Text reveals by masked words or lines (SplitText), never letter scrambles. Every image reveal uses the same 35° 'pitch-wipe' clip-path as the 3D roof pitch; this is the site-wide signature. The red line is the only animated colour: it draws section dividers, form progress and hotspot leaders. Durations: micro 150-200 ms, UI 600-900 ms, 3D beats scroll-scrubbed (scrub 0.8). Scroll: Lenis lerp 0.09 on desktop, native scrolling on touch. prefers-reduced-motion: no pin, no smooth scroll, stills plus opacity fades only.
croatianHeadlines: Od letve do sljemena.
Krov se ne radi odoka.
Vani pljušti. Kod vas suho.
Svaki šaraf na svom mjestu.

photoPlan: REALITY CHECK: all 19 photos are WhatsApp exports (1200x1600 or 900x1600, 170-510 KB). They are fine for cards but too small and too compressed for full-bleed desktop. Before anything else, ask for the phone originals through a Google Photos or iCloud 'original quality' link, not WhatsApp or Viber. PLACEMENT: 17 (golden hour, snow guards) is the 'Ovo nije render' match-cut full-bleed, the OG/social image and the hero of the Limeni krovovi page. 1 (valley flashing, worker on the ridge) is the 'uvala' hotspot in Detalji and the Popravak page image. 8 (clad chimney with barrel cap) is the inset card in the hero chimney beat, the Dimnjaci page image and a Detalji hotspot. 10 (flat roof with Zagreb/Medvednica panorama) is the 'Gdje radimo' background and the Opšavi/ravni krovovi card. 4 (trapez field inside the capping, street) is the Opšavi page hero and appears in Radovi. 5 (snow guards, crisp sky) is the Snjegobrani card and the configurator's 'real example'. 7 (mitered V-corner) is the Detalji craft close-up, cropped tight and darkened at the edges to hide the messy yard. 13 and 12 go in Radovi. 16 and 18 (standing seam) go on the Falcani lim card/page; 16 keeps the drill as 'work in progress' authenticity. 6 (worker at a junction) is the human shot in 'Kako radimo'. 2, 3, 11, 19 and 20 are for case studies and the 'Montaža' step (tools on gravel reads as honest). 14 and 15: do not use (finger and shadow). 9: redraw as a vector. TREATMENT: one Lightroom preset for every photo (neutral-cool white balance, +shadows, -highlights, light clarity, no HDR look). Crop to 4:5 for cards and 9:16 for mobile/stories. Heal protective-film residue and fingerprints only; never retouch the workmanship itself. EXTRA SHOOT (one day with a photographer and a licensed drone operator, or spread over the next 2-3 jobs): (a) Drone at golden hour over one finished pitched roof and one flat-roof job: top-down rise, slow 180° orbit, and a pull-back from the ridge to the neighbourhood with Medvednica, in 4K60, both 16:9 and 9:16. The operator must be registered with the HACZ and respect the Zagreb airport control zones and the neighbours' privacy. (b) A timelapse of one full roof replacement from a fixed high point (old phone or GoPro on a clamp, 1 frame every 5-10 s, across all days). This becomes 'Tri dana u 15 sekundi' and proves the 3D story is real. (c) Before/after pairs taken from the exact same marked spot, for repair work. (d) Craft macro clips, 3-5 s at 60/120 fps: a sheet in the bending brake (savijačica), a seamer closing a falc, a screw with its EPDM washer biting in, a cap being riveted. These become muted micro-loops in the service cards. (e) A team portrait in workwear by the van, one shot on a roof in harnesses (safety sells), and an owner portrait for O nama. (f) A flat sample of their actual RAL 7016 sheet photographed in sun and in overcast, as the reference for matching the 3D steel material. RULES: peel the protective film before final shots, clean the lens, shoot every hero view in both landscape and portrait, no 0.5x ultra-wide for heroes, and shoot at golden hour or in bright overcast.

performancePlan: RULE: the 3D is a progressive enhancement that never touches LCP. BUDGETS (mobile, 4G, Moto G/Galaxy A class): LCP ≤ 2.0 s, CLS ≤ 0.05, INP ≤ 200 ms. Critical path ≤ 180 KB: HTML, inlined critical CSS, 2 preloaded woff2 subsets, and the hero poster AVIF (~70 KB portrait / ~90 KB landscape, art-directed <picture>, fetchpriority=high). The poster is rendered from the same scene, so the canvas crossfades in pixel-identically once its first frame has rendered. 3D LOADING: only Tier A/B ever download 3D, through a dynamic import after window load + requestIdleCallback or after the first scroll/touch, whichever comes first. 3D payload ≤ 700 KB total. JS ≤ 260 KB gzip (three tree-shaken, R3F, only the drei modules used, CSM); postprocessing is a separate chunk for desktop only. GLB ≤ 250 KB with meshopt + quantization (the meshopt decoder is tiny, unlike Draco's WASM). At most 2 WebP textures, ≤ 150 KB (membrane print, step/screw normal map). No HDR file: the environment is procedural Lightformers. RUNTIME: ≤ 40 draw calls, because everything repeated is an InstancedMesh. ≤ 250k triangles on desktop and ≤ 70k on mobile, where the crijep-lim steps become a normal map. Shadows are baked once (frames=1) and there are no realtime shadow maps. DPR clamped to [1, 1.75] on desktop and [1, 1.5] on mobile. PerformanceMonitor + AdaptiveDpr degrade quality, with automatic fallback to stills under 30 fps. frameloop='demand' plus IntersectionObserver stop rendering once the hero and configurator are off-screen. During scroll, GSAP writes only to refs and uniforms, never to React state. A webglcontextlost handler swaps to the poster. Use svh units and ignoreMobileResize so the iOS address bar can't break the pin. REST OF SITE: static Astro HTML with zero JS by default. Images through <Picture> as AVIF/WebP with srcset, lazy below the fold, with blur placeholders. Video loops ≤ 1.2 MB (H.264 + AV1), poster first, preload=none, playing only in view. No Google Maps embed (static SVG map), no chat widgets, no cookie-based trackers, so there is no consent wall. QA on real devices: iPhone 12 Safari, Galaxy A54, a Redmi Note with a Mali GPU, and an old Intel UHD laptop. Lighthouse CI budgets fail the build if they regress.
risks: Scope: polishing the scroll choreography can eat weeks. Lock the storyboard in week 1, build the Tier C stills hero first so the site is always shippable, and timebox the 3D to about 12 dev days. Strongly consider launching Phase 1 with the stills hero and turning the 3D on in Phase 2 behind the same poster.
Mid-range Android GPUs (Mali) and thermal throttling can make a long pin janky and hot. Mitigate with device tiers, lite mode, PerformanceMonitor auto-fallback and the shorter 380svh mobile pin.

iOS Safari quirks: address-bar resizes break pins, the WebGL context is lost when the tab is backgrounded, and memory is capped. Mitigate with svh units, ignoreMobileResize, a context-loss handler and tiny textures.

Cheap-looking 3D destroys the premium impression faster than having no 3D. Don't attempt photorealism. Spend the time on lighting and materials, match the steel against a real sheet sample, and get the client to approve one still frame before animating anything.

Craft accuracy: roofers and informed homeowners will spot a wrong build order. For example, falc needs full boarding plus a separating layer, and batten spacing follows the sheet manufacturer. The owner must sign off on the layer stack and on every caption.

A long pinned intro is a problem for people who only want to call. Keep the sticky call/WhatsApp/Viber CTAs visible throughout, plus 'Preskoči animaciju', step-counter jump links, and a total pin of at most 640vh on desktop.

SEO and accessibility: text inside a canvas is invisible. All headlines and captions must be real HTML, the canvas aria-hidden, a keyboard skip link provided, and the reduced-motion path fully usable.

Weak source assets: WhatsApp-compressed photos with protective film and scratches, and an AI-generated raster logo with brushed-metal effects. The logo needs a vector redraw, and its ownability should be checked.
Content truth: years in business, number of roofs, warranty and reviews must come from the client. Placeholder numbers must not ship.
Drone footage in Zagreb needs a registered operator, airport control-zone clearance (Pleso/Lučko) and respect for neighbours' privacy.
Library churn (R3F/drei major versions, React versions). Pin exact versions and keep all 3D isolated in one island so it can be swapped or switched off.

name: NACRT → LIM (Blueprint → Steel): 'Mjera do milimetra'
oneLiner: The whole site works like a technical drawing that comes to life. Every roof starts as a dimensioned redline sketch on millimetre paper. A virtual abkant press bends it into anthracite steel, and then it turns into a real Karamatić job. Most Croatian roofers say 'kvalitetno i povoljno'. This brand instead sells one loud, provable idea in the American style: MJERA DO MILIMETRA. My opinion: the drawing language is the hook, and the real photos, a phone number visible at all times and plain Croatian copy do the selling.

heroStoryboard.beat: 12-col grid on graphite #0E1013 with a CSS millimetre grid (no images). The left 5 columns hold the mono eyebrow 'LIMARSKI RADOVI · ZAGREB I OKOLICA', the H1 'SEDAM PUTA MJERIMO. JEDNOM SAVIJEMO.', a subline, a red CTA 'Besplatna procjena', an outline CTA 'Pošalji slike na WhatsApp' and a mono trust row ('★ [4,9] Google · [600]+ krovova · jamstvo [10] god.', placeholders until the client confirms). The right 7 columns hold a 'drawing sheet' (inline SVG, viewBox 0 0 1200 900) that bleeds off the right edge, with a sastavnica (title block) in its bottom-right corner. A vertical mm scroll-ruler runs down the far right edge. The H1 is already painted at t=0 and is NEVER animated from opacity 0, so it counts as the LCP element.

The sheet frame draws clockwise from the top-left (DrawSVG 0→100%, power2.inOut). Corner registration crosshairs scale 0→1 (0.2s, stagger 0.05). Title-block cells rule in, and mono fields type in with SplitText chars (stagger 0.012): 'LIMARIJA KARAMATIĆ · CRTEŽ 001 · MJERILO 1:50 · LIST 1/1 · STATUS: —'.

Construction and house linework. Dashed axes sweep in: the ground line left→right, then the symmetry axis bottom→top (0.5s). Then walls, the main gable, the window cross, the chimney and the second gable (the same oblique 2.5D house as the logo) draw with DrawSVG: stroke #D5DBDF, 1.25px non-scaling-stroke, stagger 0.06, power1.inOut. A 6px red pen-dot rides the leading edge of each path like a plotter head (position from getPointAtLength in onUpdate).

Redline dimensioning. Three dimension lines grow from their midpoints (scaleX 0→1, 0.45s, power3.out) with 45° tick ends popping in, and extension lines drop down. Values count up in IBM Plex Mono #FF3B3F with tabular-nums: '12 450', '7 800'. A pitch arc draws, followed by '35°'. Leader lines with circled ①–④ draw out to the snjegobran, sljeme, opšav dimnjaka and oluk positions, and their labels type in.

Flat sheet. Above the walls, a flat parallelogram sheet draws in outline, labelled 'RAZVIJENA ŠIRINA 6 240 mm', with a dashed red fold line on its centre and 'PREGIB · 2× 35°'. It slides down 24px onto the fold axis (0.3s, power2.out).

The press beam drops from above the frame along two guide rails: y −260→0 in 0.16s, power4.in. The beam is a black upper tool whose die tip is the red Λ taken from the 'A' in KARAMATIĆ. On contact, the sheet MorphSVGs from flat to Λ: the two halves rotate about the ridge in 0.22s with CustomEase 'press' (fast in, hard stop, 2% recoil). A 1px white flash line runs along the ridge (opacity 1→0, 0.15s). The whole sheet group recoils y +2→0 (0.12s). The beam then retracts (0.35s, power2.out) and fades, and a red mono tick '✓ 35° · ±0,5 mm' blips beside the ridge for 0.8s.

The folded Λ drops 40px onto the walls with the press ease. Roof faces then fill with brushed anthracite (a <pattern> tile) via a clipPath rect sweeping eave→ridge (0.35s, stagger 0.1). The front plane is #2B3034 and the side plane #383E42, which sells the 2.5D. Standing-seam lines draw ridge→eave (DrawSVG, stagger 0.015). Linework under the steel darkens from #D5DBDF to #1A1D20, so the drawing becomes an object.

Trim. The red brand stripe under the eaves draws in (DrawSVG, #D7141A, 3px), exactly as in the logo. The gutter extrudes (scaleX from the left) and the downpipe drops (scaleY, 0.25s). The chimney cladding fills and its cap mini-folds (MorphSVG, 0.18s press). Snow guards pop in row by row (scale 0→1, stagger 0.03).

Glint and stamp. One specular band (linearGradient #E8ECEF at 0→22%→0 opacity) sweeps diagonally across all steel faces via gradientTransform (0.6s, power2.inOut). Dimensions and callouts dim to 40%, so they stay as a ghost overlay. A red 'IZVEDENO' rubber stamp lands in the title block: scale 1.4→1, rotate −6°, 0.14s, with a 1px ink double-offset.

Pointer parallax applies only on desktop with pointer:fine: grid ±3px, linework ±6px, steel ±10px and callouts ±14px, each via gsap.quickTo (0.6s). Over the drawing only, the cursor becomes a crosshair with a live mono X/Y readout. A '↻ PONOVI CRTEŽ' mono button in the title block replays the intro. The intro never blocks scroll: if the user scrolls before 4.5s, the timeline jumps to progress(1) over 0.3s.

Reality bleeds in. Photo 17 (golden hour, AVIF, fetched after window load) fades in inside an SVG <mask> made of the same roof-face polygons. The steel texture under it fades out (1→0), and the linework turns white at 70%. The drawing now IS the real roof.

The mask path MorphSVGs from the roof shape to the full drawing-sheet rectangle, and the photo counter-zooms 1.12→1. Callouts ① and ③ re-target their leader-line endpoints onto real features in 17: the snow guards at about (83%, 62%) and the brick chimney at about (49%, 17%). The title block updates to 'STATUS: IZVEDENO · ZAGREB · 2025' (placeholder).
Hand-off. The H1 column moves y −12vh and opacity 1→0.25. The scroll-ruler readout reaches '1 200 mm'. The next section's dimension chain starts drawing at the bottom edge, then the hero unpins.

heroMobileFallback: This mode applies below 1024px or with pointer:coarse, switched via gsap.matchMedia. Layout order: a 56px header, then the drawing panel at 100vw × 46svh (the SVG viewBox switches to a centred 900×900 crop of the house), then the eyebrow, H1, subline and two CTAs. On a 360×740 screen all of that is visible at first paint. A sticky bottom bar (Nazovi / WhatsApp / Ponuda, 64px, safe-area aware) is present from t=0 and is never animated in. The 'short' intro takes 3.2s: frame 0–0.25s → house linework 0.2–1.0s (no construction axes, no pen-dot) → 2 dimensions + 2 callouts 0.9–1.4s → abkant hit 1.4–1.75s (kept: it is the signature and costs almost nothing) → steel fill + seams 1.75–2.5s → red stripe + glint + IZVEDENO stamp 2.5–3.2s. There is no pin, no scrub, no pointer parallax, no custom cursor and no photo inside the hero, which saves about 80KB. The next block is the 'Iz nacrta na krov' card instead: photo 17 (800w AVIF) with the same white linework and callouts, which wipe in once on enter (clip-path, 0.6s). Tapping the drawing replays it. The intro is skipped and the finished frame is shown when any of these is true: prefers-reduced-motion, navigator.connection.saveData, deviceMemory ≤ 2, hardwareConcurrency ≤ 4, or the intro has already played this session (sessionStorage). Without JS, the finished drawing is the default markup, so nothing breaks.
heroTech:
One inline SVG (viewBox 0 0 1200 900, about 35KB raw / 10KB gzip) authored in Figma or Illustrator from the vector redraw of the logo house. It uses an oblique 2.5D view: chimney on the left, main gable, standing-seam plane, second gable on the right, gutter and downpipe. The hero is literally the logo being built.

Layer groups with IDs: #grid, #frame, #titleblock, #construct, #house-lines, #dims, #callouts, #flat-sheet (two polygons, halfL/halfR), #press-beam (bar + guide rails + red Λ die), #roof-faces, #seams, #trim (red stripe, gutter, downpipe, chimney cladding/cap), #snowguards, #glint, #stamp and #photo-mask. In #roof-faces each polygon is filled with a <pattern> holding one 512px brushed-anthracite AVIF tile, plus a per-face shade overlay. #glint is a <linearGradient> animated via gradientTransform. #photo-mask is a <mask> that reuses the roof-face paths, with an <image> whose href is set to 17.avif after load. All strokes use vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke.

The markup ships in the FINISHED state. An inline head script adds html.js-anim, and gsap.set() rewinds the layers to empty before the SVG becomes visible. [data-anim] hides it until then, with a 300ms failsafe.

Libraries: GSAP 3.13+ (all plugins free since the 2025 Webflow change): core, DrawSVGPlugin (strokes), MorphSVGPlugin (flat sheet → Λ roof, chimney cap, roof mask → rect), SplitText (title block and labels), CustomEase ('press' = M0,0 C0.5,0 0.62,0.98 0.8,1.02 0.9,1.03 0.95,1 1,1), ScrollTrigger (desktop pin + scrub only) and gsap.quickTo (parallax). The pen-dot uses getPointAtLength, so MotionPathPlugin is not needed. A single buildIntro(mode) function returns one master timeline in 'full' (4.5s), 'short' (3.2s) or 'none' mode. Own code is vanilla TypeScript, about 8KB, with no React. No WebGL and no canvas. A canvas glint is an optional fallback only if Safari stutters on the gradient animation.

typography:
Two fonts, both free, self-hosted, and supporting latin-ext, so č ć ž š đ and Č Ć Ž Š Đ are fully covered.

1) ARCHIVO (Google Fonts / Fontsource variable, axes wght 100–900 + wdth 62–125) for everything human:
- H1: wdth 125 / wght 800, UPPERCASE, clamp(2.4rem, 7.2vw, 6.75rem), line-height 0.9, tracking −0.01em. It echoes the wide, heavy 'KARAMATIĆ' wordmark. Below 400px, use wdth 110 so 'SAVIJEMO.' fits.
- H2: wdth 115 / 700, sentence case, clamp(1.9rem, 4vw, 3.5rem).
- Body: wdth 100 / 400, 17–18px, line-height 1.55.
- Buttons: wdth 112 / 700, uppercase, 15px, tracking 0.04em.

2) IBM PLEX MONO (Google Fonts, latin-ext; 400 + 500) for the technical layer: dimensions, callouts, eyebrows ('02 — USLUGE'), title blocks, prices and the phone number. Set at 11–13px, uppercase, tracking 0.08em, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums slashed-zero.

Croatian technical conventions: decimal comma (0,6 mm), thin-space thousands (12 450 mm), „ “ quotes, and '45 €/m²' with a space.

Deliberately avoid Montserrat, Poppins and Open Sans: that is what every Croatian contractor site already uses.
texturesAndMotion:
SURFACES. Sections alternate between graphite night sheets (#0E1013 with a mm grid: 8px minor lines at 4%, 40px major at 8%, via repeating-linear-gradient, no images) and paper sheets (#EEECE7 with a #D8D3C8 grid). Scrolling feels like leafing through a project folder. Section boundaries are 35° diagonal 'fold' edges (clip-path polygon), the same pitch as the hero roof, with + registration crosshairs at the corners.

Brushed anthracite (one pre-rendered 512px AVIF tile, about 15KB, horizontal streaks) appears ONLY where something has been 'built': the hero roof faces, hovered service cards and the primary button hover. It is never a page background, because that reads as 2008-cheap. Red is redline only: dimensions, callout numbers, stamps and CTAs. No grain, no glassmorphism, no gradients except the steel glint. The look is crisp vector, like a plotter output.

MOTION GRAMMAR: 'measure, then cut'.
(1) Everything first appears as a 1px line (DrawSVG, or scaleX on rules).
(2) Only then does it fill.

There are only two eases:
- 'draft' = power2.inOut, 0.6–0.9s, for lines.
- 'press' = a CustomEase with a fast entry, hard stop and about 2% recoil, 0.18–0.3s, for every fill, fold, snap and stamp.

Other rules:
- H2s use SplitText line masks (yPercent 105→0, 0.7s, stagger 0.08). The H1 is never animated.
- Numbers count up with tabular-nums.
- Photos use the scan reveal (clip-path with a red scanline leading edge), at most 6% parallax, and no Ken Burns.
- Links get dimension-line underlines with tick ends.
- Buttons physically depress on :active (translateY 2px, shadow collapses).
- The crosshair cursor with an X/Y readout appears only over drawings and only with pointer:fine.
- No scroll-jacking on touch devices.
- prefers-reduced-motion renders every SVG in its final state, keeping only ≤150ms opacity fades.

photoPlan:
GET THE ORIGINALS FIRST. The supplied files are 1200×1600 WhatsApp copies, and all are portrait except 15. Ask for full-resolution originals via Google Drive or WeTransfer. They should be the iPhone 3024×4032 or larger files.

EDITING. Use one Lightroom preset, 'Antracit': neutral white balance around 5600K, highlights −30, shadows +15, clarity +8, upright and lens correction. Keep the neighbours' red tiles saturated, because they are the perfect complement to the anthracite and the brand red. Heal protective-film residue, scuffs and swarf on the sheets (visible in 7, 17, 4 and 1), since homeowners read them as dirty or scratched work. Remove fingers and the photographer's shadow. Never fake workmanship or replace skies.

PLACEMENT:
- 17: hero photo inside the roof mask (desktop scroll) and the mobile 'Iz nacrta na krov' card. Also the OG/social image, cropped 1200×630 at y≈420–1050.
- 4: Nacrt↔Izvedeno slider #1 (the geometric flat roof is the easiest to trace) and the hero of the 'Ravni krovovi i opšavi atika' page.
- 7: slider #2 and the 'mjera do milimetra' precision macro. The mitered V corner is the proof shot. Crop tight to the sheet and lose the messy garden.
- 8: slider #3, the 'Dimnjaci' service, and the anatomy layer 'opšav dimnjaka i kapa'.
- 10: the 'Područje rada' panel 'Pogled s krova na Medvednicu' (4:3 crop at y≈250–1150), slider #4, and O nama.
- 1: hero of the 'Limeni krovovi' service page (the worker on the ridge gives human scale) and the anatomy layer 'uvala'. Crop the bottom 12% to remove the shadow.
- 5: anatomy 'snjegobrani', the 'Oluci i snjegobrani' service, and the radovi grid.
- 6: anatomy 'spoj krovnih ploha' and the 'Popravci' page.
- 16 and 18: 'Falcani krovovi'. In 16 the drill and roof hook show honest work in progress.
- 2, 3, 11, 19, 20: gallery on the atika page. Use 20 (tools on gravel) for Proces step 05.
- 12, 13: radovi grid filler.
- 14, 15: do not use (finger, shadow).
- 9: only a reference for the vector logo redraw.

SHOT LIST FOR THE CLIENT (about 1 golden-hour day, a half-day in the workshop, and 1 drone day):
1) Drone, flown by a licensed operator. Nadir (straight-down 90°) shots of 4–6 finished roofs: these map 1:1 onto plan-view line drawings, which gives perfect Nacrt↔Izvedeno overlays and a possible future plan-view hero variant. Also slow 45° orbits (4K, 10–15s) and one rising reveal with Medvednica behind.
2) Workshop. The abkant press bending RAL 7016 sheet: 4K at 120fps slow motion, side-on and die close-up, 5–10s clips. Also the sheet sliding out and stacks of finished profiles. These feed Proces step 04, O nama and Reels/TikTok.
3) Timelapse of one complete roof (GoPro on a neighbouring roof or tripod, 1 frame every 5–10s across the whole job). It becomes a 90-frame scroll-scrub sequence on desktop and an 8s MP4 on mobile.
4) Before/after pairs from the same marked spot on every job from now on. These feed the caliper slider's 'Prije ↔ Poslije' mode.
5) Detail macros after peeling the film: falc seam, okapnica, rivets, snjegobran, gutter bracket, chimney cap. Shoot side-lit at golden hour so the folds read.
6) People. An owner portrait and the crew in branded workwear (graphite with a red stripe) in front of the van. Also a hands shot with a tape measure or laser meter on a sheet, which carries the 'mjera' story.
7) Rule for every hero-worthy angle: shoot it twice, once in landscape 4:3 and once in portrait 3:4, with the 1× lens. The 0.5× ultra-wide used in 4 and 10 bends the parapets.

performancePlan:
BUDGETS. Measured with the Lighthouse mobile Moto G Power/4G profile plus a real Samsung A-series phone:
- LCP ≤ 2.0s, CLS ≤ 0.05, INP ≤ 150ms, TBT ≤ 150ms.
- Home JS ≤ 85KB gzip: GSAP core ~27 + ScrollTrigger ~12 + DrawSVG ~2 + MorphSVG ~9 + SplitText ~6 + CustomEase ~2 + Flip ~5, plus about 8KB of own code.
- Hero SVG ≤ 12KB gzip, inlined.
- Mobile first-load transfer ≤ 700KB.

LCP. The LCP element is the text H1, painted immediately and never faded in from opacity 0. The hero has NO raster image at first paint.

FONTS. One custom subset per family: Basic Latin + ČčĆćĐđŠšŽž + € „ “ – —. That gives Archivo variable at about 40KB and Plex Mono at 2 × ~15KB. Preload Archivo only. Use font-display: swap with a fontaine size-adjusted fallback, so there is no CLS.

SCRIPT LOADING. GSAP is a deferred module. The intro starts on requestAnimationFrame after DOMContentLoaded and does not wait for fonts (300ms cap).

ANIMATION COST.
- Animate only transform, opacity, stroke-dashoffset and the attributes of small SVG elements.
- No animated SVG filters (feTurbulence was rejected in favour of the pre-rendered texture tile).
- will-change is set only during tweens.
- Pins exist only under gsap.matchMedia('(min-width:1024px) and (pointer:fine)').
- ScrollTrigger.config({ignoreMobileResize:true}), with svh/dvh units.

IMAGES. Astro <Picture> with AVIF + WebP at 480/800/1200w, explicit width/height, loading=lazy and decoding=async, and an anthracite dominant-colour placeholder. The hero photo 17 (about 90KB AVIF) is requested after window load with fetchpriority=low.

VIDEO. The abkant slow-mo and the timelapse never appear in the hero. They use preload=none, play/pause via IntersectionObserver, are 720p H.264 + WebM at ≤ 2MB, and have AVIF posters. The 90-frame timelapse scrub is desktop-only and lazy (about 3MB WebP total).

THIRD PARTIES. Nothing render-blocking:
- No Google Maps iframe: a static SVG map plus a deep link instead.
- Reviews are fetched at build time.
- Analytics are cookieless.
- Turnstile loads only when the form gets focus.

LITE MODE. When saveData, deviceMemory ≤ 2 or hardwareConcurrency ≤ 4 is detected: skip the intro, disable parallax, the ruler and the cursor, and cap images at 800w.

QA. Lighthouse CI budgets on every deploy. WebPageTest 'Moto G4 – 4G – Frankfurt' before launch. A day-2 spike to test iOS Safari SVG <mask> + MorphSVG and the gradient glint before anything else is built.
risks: Photo resolution and orientation: every supplied shot is 1200×1600 (WhatsApp-compressed) and portrait, so they cannot carry full-bleed 16:9 desktop panels. This direction deliberately frames photos in portrait/4:5 panels ≤ 1200px wide and makes the SVG drawing the hero. Still, get the originals and book a landscape/drone shoot.

The custom SVG work is the critical path: the hero house, fold geometry, 6 profile details, 4 traced 'nacrt' overlays and the exploded anatomy add up to about 6–7 days of drawing. If the dev isn't fluent in Illustrator or Figma vectors, hire an illustrator for 2–3 days or push the anatomy section to phase 2.

A 2D MorphSVG fold can look cheap and flat if it is unlit. Do a one-day spike first (flat sheet → Λ with per-face shading, the glint and the press ease) and show the client a screen recording before building the rest.

The blueprint aesthetic can feel cold or 'architect-y' to older homeowners. Balance it with plain Croatian copy, real faces (crew photo), the warm golden-hour photo 17, a phone number that is always visible, and price ranges and guarantees. The drawing is the hook, not the content.

Over-animation can cost conversions and accessibility. CTAs must be visible at t=0, the intro must be ≤ 4.5s and interruptible, there must be no scroll-jacking on touch, plus a full prefers-reduced-motion path, visible focus states and a keyboard-operable caliper slider. Older users on cheap Androids are a real segment.

The logo is a glossy, AI-style raster with 3D effects. It clashes with the crisp linework and will not scale to a favicon or a van. It needs a vector redraw: a flat lockup, a line version and the Λ monogram. The client may be attached to the gloss, so pitch it as 'the same logo, made for web, van and workwear'. Also check that the AI logo is not a near-copy of a stock design.

Every number on the site is a placeholder until the client confirms it: years, roof count, Google rating, warranty, prices, the 48h/same-day promises and whether they own an abkant workshop. Never ship invented numbers or reviews. Sections hide via CMS flags until the facts are real.
Safari/iOS: an SVG <mask> with an <image> inside a scrubbed MorphSVG can drop frames or flash. Fall back to a simple crossfade over the drawing on WebKit if testing shows under 50fps.

Content depends on client shoots: the before/after mode, abkant video and timelapse all need them. Launch must not wait for those assets, so the caliper ships first in 'Nacrt ↔ Izvedeno' mode using traced drawings of the existing photos.

Drone legality: operators in Croatia must register with HACZ (the civil aviation agency), and much of Zagreb is near the controlled airspace around Zagreb Airport (Pleso). Hire a licensed local operator.

Scope: the full direction is about 32 dev-days. A realistic MVP launch takes about 22 days: hero, core home sections, 6 service pages, the radovi grid and the quote form. The anatomy explode, the process timelapse scrub, case-study pages and the blog become phase 2.

Contrast on dark UI read outdoors in sunlight: keep body text ≥ 7:1 (#D5DBDF on #0E1013). Small red text must use #FF3B3F on dark or #B80F15 on paper. Use the brand #D7141A only for buttons with white text and for large elements.

name: ANTRACIT PRO: "Krov za 60 sekundi", the quote-first contractor playbook
oneLiner: A US-grade lead machine in Karamatić's own anthracite and red. An illustrated roof builds itself layer by layer, then turns into a real Zagreb roof (photo 17). Every screen offers a 60-second price range, one-tap Call/WhatsApp and hard proof: real reviews, a written warranty and real projects. My opinion: what makes it look ultra-premium is restraint, speed and authentic work, not heavy 3D. Croatian contractor sites lose on trust and friction, not on effects. Animations here exist only to make the work look precise and to pull people into the quote.

heroStoryboard.beat: Server-rendered split hero on a 12-col grid. LEFT (5 cols, ink #0E1012 bg): eyebrow 'LIMARIJA · ZAGREB I OKOLICA' (Archivo wdth 125, tracking 0.18em, echoes the spaced LIMARIJA wordmark). Static H1 'Krov kao nacrtan.' with no load animation, because it is the LCP element. Sub-line, an address input 'Upišite adresu objekta' with a red button 'Okvirna cijena za 60 s', secondary links 'Nazovi 0xx xxx xxxx' and 'WhatsApp', and 3 trust chips (Google rating, 'Pisana garancija', 'Odgovor isti dan'). Everything is clickable at t=0. RIGHT (7 cols, graphite stage #121416 with faint standing-seam hairline pattern): only the house body is visible. Off-white planes in the logo silhouette (main gable, chimney, side gable, window), with the empty roof outline at 20% opacity.

12 rafters (#8A9299, 1.5px) draw eave to ridge with DrawSVG, stagger 0.04, power2.out. In the copy column, the only motion is a 4px red underline (#D7141A) under 'nacrtan' (scaleX 0→1, 0.6s). Trust chips rise 8px and fade in, stagger 0.06.
Membrane: a pale grey sheet unrolls down each roof plane from the ridge (scaleY 0→1, transform-origin top, power3.out), with a faint diagonal sheen gliding across it.
Battens: 9 horizontal laths snap in bottom-up, stagger 0.035, back.out(2) with a 2px overshoot. This gives the carpentry rhythm.

Metal panels: 6 tile-profile strips (fill #383E42, wave strokes #2A2F33, 1px highlight #5A6268) drop from y:-48px, opacity 0→1, stagger 0.14, power3.out with a 2px settle. When a strip lands, its screw dots ripple in (scale 0→1, 0.01s stagger). The side gable fills with standing-seam panels (vertical seams), a nod to falcani lim.
The ridge cap (sljemenjak) runs along the ridge left to right (scaleX). The valley flashing between the two roof bodies draws on (DrawSVG).
Chimney: anthracite cladding wipes up over the brick (clip-path inset, bottom-up), then the metal chimney cap drops 20px with back.out(3). Three rows of snow guards pop in, stagger 0.05.
The gutter draws along both eaves and the downpipe extends down (scaleY 0→1). Then the logo's red eave stripe (#D7141A, 4px) draws along the eaves. This is the brand signature beat.

One specular sheen sweeps across the finished roof: a white-to-transparent linear gradient at 18% opacity and -20°, translateX -100%→200%, 0.75s, power2.inOut. It reads as new coated steel catching the sun.

ILLUSTRATION-TO-REALITY REVEAL. The roof polygon becomes a CSS clip-path window. Photo 17 (golden-hour crijep-lim with snow guards, AVIF) fades in inside the roof shape at scale 1.08→1 while the illustration fades out. Then the clip-path polygon morphs from the roof shape to the full stage rectangle (radius 20px), power4.inOut 0.9s. A caption chip slides in bottom-left: 'Ovo nije ilustracija. · Zagreb · crijep-lim RAL 7016 · 4 dana', with 'Pogledaj projekt →'.

Slow Ken Burns on the photo (scale 1→1.04 over 14s, yoyo). 3 hotspot dots fade in (sljeme, snjegobrani, opšav); tap or hover shows a tooltip linking to that service. A CMS-driven availability chip '● 3 slobodna termina za izmjeru ovaj tjedan' pulses once. It is hidden if the field is empty, so it is never fake.

Focus or click on the address field or any CTA calls timeline.progress(1), which jumps to the final photo state, and opens estimator step 2 inline. A buyer never waits for an animation. A visually hidden 'Preskoči animaciju' button serves keyboard users. With prefers-reduced-motion, the final state renders immediately.

At 80px the header goes from transparent to solid #0E1012 at 90% with backdrop-blur. The stage photo parallaxes y 0→-6% (ScrollTrigger scrub 0.5). The proof bar (Google rating, years, finished roofs, supplier logos) rises 48px over the hero's bottom edge. At 60vh a floating 'Besplatna procjena' pill appears bottom-right (desktop only).

Below 768px the hero is text-first, so LCP is the H1 text and lands in about 1.5s on 4G.
- 56px header: flat vector logo, phone icon (tel:), menu.
- Eyebrow, then the H1 'Krov kao nacrtan.' (Archivo 800, wdth 112, 40–44px, line-height 1.0), then one sub-line.

- No parallax, no Lenis and no hover hotspots on touch. Hotspots become a tappable 'Što vidite na slici?' list under the photo.
heroTech:
Inline SVG isometric house, hand-built in Figma or Illustrator as a vector redraw of the logo house. Layers are grouped with IDs: #walls #rafters #membrane #battens #panels > .strip #screws #ridge #valley #chimney-clad #chimney-cap #snowguards #gutter #downpipe #eave-red #sheen. About 30–40KB gzipped, inlined in the HTML so it costs no extra request.

It is animated by one GSAP 3 timeline. GSAP and all its plugins are free since 2025; this uses DrawSVGPlugin for rafters, valley, gutter and the red line, and MorphSVGPlugin for the roof-pitch morph reused in the estimator. Only transform, opacity, stroke-dashoffset and clip-path are animated, so there is no layout thrash.

The reveal is a CSS clip-path: polygon() on the photo wrapper, tweened by GSAP from the roof-polygon points to the stage rectangle. Photo 17 is served through Astro <Picture> (AVIF/WebP, fetchpriority=low, decoded after LCP).

The same SVG component is reused as the estimator's progress visual, so it is built once and used twice. No WebGL, no Three.js and no video in v1.

v2, once the client films it: swap the reveal target for a 6s muted drone or timelapse loop of a real roof replacement. Encode AV1/HEVC with an H.264 fallback, ≤1.2MB, with photo 17 as poster. The illustration intro stays.

typography:
DISPLAY: Archivo, a Google Font variable font with wght 100–900 and a wdth 62–125 axis. Load the latin + latin-ext subsets, which give full Č Ć Ž Š Đ / č ć ž š đ.
- The wide, heavy cut matches the logo's 'KARAMATIĆ' and has the bold American contractor feel without a paid font.
- H1: wght 800, wdth 115, letter-spacing -0.02em, line-height 0.95, clamp(40px, 6.2vw, 96px), sentence case for readability.
- Eyebrows and labels: UPPERCASE, wdth 125, wght 600, tracking 0.18em, 12–13px. This echoes the spaced 'L I M A R I J A'. Leave line-height ≥ 1.1 on uppercase so Č and Ć accents don't clip.
- Prices and stats: wght 700 with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Croatian number format '12.400 €' and decimal comma '0,5 mm'.

BODY / UI: Inter variable (latin-ext). 16px/1.6 on mobile, 17px on desktop, weights 400/500/600; buttons 600 at 16px.

SPEC LABELS: IBM Plex Mono 500 (latin-ext), 12px uppercase, used sparingly for material specs ('RAL 7016 · 0,5 MM · 4 DANA').

Self-host all three via Fontsource (@fontsource-variable/archivo, @fontsource-variable/inter, @fontsource/ibm-plex-mono) instead of the Google Fonts CDN. That avoids the EU/GDPR Google Fonts IP issue. Subset to latin + latin-ext woff2, preload only Archivo, font-display: swap, and use metric-matched Arial fallbacks via fontaine or capsize so the swap causes zero CLS.
texturesAndMotion:
TEXTURES, all real roofing geometry rather than generic decoration:
1. Standing-seam hairline pattern: repeating-linear-gradient with a 1px Aluminij line every 56px at 6–8% opacity, on dark stages.
2. Tile-profile wave divider: the silhouette of a crijep-lim sheet edge as an SVG section divider between light and dark sections.
3. Brushed metal: one pre-rendered 512px WebP noise and horizontal-streak tile (made once with an feTurbulence baseFrequency '0.002 0.6' filter and exported). Used at 5–8% opacity on the guarantee plate and footer. Never a live SVG filter on mobile.
4. The red eave line: a 3–4px #D7141A rule that draws under key headings, the brand device lifted from the logo.

MOTION SYSTEM:
- Easing: one custom curve, cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), plus power3.out for entrances.
- Durations: 0.4–0.8s; stagger 0.04–0.08; entrance distance 16–24px max.
- Reveals fire once (ScrollTrigger once:true or IntersectionObserver).
- One hero sequence only. No scroll-jacking or pinned storytelling: conversion pages must let users reach the phone number instantly.
- Lenis smooth scroll on desktop only and optional; off on touch.
- Count-ups only on real numbers.
- Animate only transform, opacity, stroke-dashoffset and clip-path.
- prefers-reduced-motion renders final states. Every animation can be skipped by interacting.

RULE: if a motion doesn't (a) make the work look precise, (b) explain the process, or (c) pull toward the quote or call, it gets cut.
croatianHeadlines: Krov kao nacrtan. ('A roof like a drawing.' The idiom 'kao nacrtano' means flawless; it pays off the illustration-to-photo reveal. Recommended homepage H1.)
Krov više neće puštati. (Colloquial Zagreb 'krov pušta' = the roof leaks. Use as H1 for the sanacija and repair Google Ads landing page.)
Precizno do zadnjeg vijka. (Craft and detail; good with photos 7 and 8.)
Lim je naš zanat. (Short and proud. 'Zanat' carries a strong tradesman connotation in Croatian. Works as the O nama or proof-section headline.)
Novi krov. Fiksna cijena. Pisana garancija. (The American triple promise in natural Croatian; use as a sub-headline or the guarantee section H2.)

1. Drone (licensed operator, HACZ-registered; check the Pleso and Lučko CTR restrictions in Zagreb): top-down orbit and street-to-roof rise on 3 finished roofs at golden hour.
2. Timelapse of one full roof replacement, either from the drone at a fixed GPS hover point each day or a GoPro on a pole or neighboring roof, 1 frame every 10s. This becomes the v2 hero video: a real roof being built.
3. Before/after pairs: before every job, shoot 3 fixed angles (street, roof plane, detail) and repeat the exact angles after.
4. Workshop: the bending machine (abkant/savijačica) folding anthracite sheet in 120fps slow-mo, seaming tool closing a falc, close-ups of riveting.
5. Team: the owner plus crew in branded anthracite workwear with a red stripe, vans with the logo, faces visible. Trust needs people.
6. Gutters and downpipes, which are currently missing entirely.

8. Product flat-lays on dark: crijep-lim, falc and trapezoid sheet samples, a snow guard and a chimney cap, for the estimator choice cards.
9. 2–3 vertical 20s client video testimonials.

performancePlan:
TARGETS, measured on a mid-range Android (Moto G Power class) over 4G:
- LCP < 2.0s, CLS < 0.05, INP < 200ms
- Lighthouse mobile ≥ 95
- Homepage transfer < 600KB on first view

HOW:
1. The LCP element is the static H1 text, not an image, on both desktop and mobile.
2. The hero SVG (about 35KB gz) is inlined in the HTML. Photo 17 loads after LCP with fetchpriority=low, AVIF about 90KB on desktop and 70KB on mobile.
3. JS budget about 90KB gz:
   - GSAP core + ScrollTrigger + DrawSVG + MorphSVG ≈ 45KB, deferred until after first paint.
   - The estimator island hydrates with client:visible or on first interaction (≈ 25KB).
   - Leaflet (≈ 40KB) and the Places script load only when step 2 opens.
4. Fonts: 2 preloaded woff2 files subset to latin + latin-ext, swap with metric-matched fallbacks.
5. Images: explicit width and height, responsive srcset/sizes, loading=lazy below the fold, blur LQIP.
6. No third-party scripts before consent. No chat widget (WhatsApp deep link instead). No Google Maps iframe (static SVG map instead). No reviews widget (curated JSON synced from Google). CSS-only logo marquee.
7. Animations use only transform, opacity, dashoffset and clip-path. GSAP's will-change is removed after tweens.
8. Device guard: if saveData, hardwareConcurrency ≤ 4 or prefers-reduced-motion, render the final states.
9. Static CDN hosting with immutable hashed assets and HTML at the edge.
10. Verify with WebPageTest (Frankfurt, Moto G4 profile, 4G), Chrome DevTools CPU 4x throttle, and a real-device check on a cheap Samsung A-series. Add a Lighthouse CI budget in GitHub Actions so regressions fail the build.
risks: The client may refuse to show prices; Croatian trades often do. Fallback: the estimator shows m², recommended material, duration ('Izvedba 3–5 dana') and books a free izmjera with no price. Or show ranges only for repairs, opšav and oluci. Either way, the client must supply a realistic €/m² matrix, and every result carries 'Okvirna procjena nije ponuda'.

Social proof must be real. If the Google profile has few reviews, run a review campaign before launch (QR card left after each job plus an SMS or WhatsApp link to the review form). Never invent counts like '500+ krovova'. Note that self-hosted review stars generally won't show as rich results for LocalBusiness.
The before/after section needs photos that don't exist yet. Ship it hidden and start the 'shoot before and after on every job' habit now.
The current logo is an AI-looking raster 3D render. It won't hold up at header or favicon sizes and will look cheap next to a premium UI. Budget 1–2 days for a vector redraw (flat and mono versions).

US-style pressure tactics (pop-ups, countdown timers, fake 'only today' scarcity) backfire with Croatian buyers and can breach EU unfair-commercial-practice rules. Scarcity must be CMS-driven and true, otherwise hidden.

GDPR and ePrivacy: a consent banner is needed for GA4, Ads and Clarity. The lead form needs a privacy notice. Addresses, phone numbers and uploaded roof photos are personal data, so set a retention policy and use EU-region storage where possible.

Satellite roof drawing is fiddly on small phones, and orthophoto age and parallax reduce accuracy. Always offer house-size presets, and treat area as an estimate. The DGU WMS terms and attribution must be checked.
Photo quality: phone shots with film residue, smudges and fingers. Without one professional photo + drone day and consistent grading, the 'ultra-premium' promise fails no matter how good the code is.
Drone filming in Zagreb is regulated (HACZ registration, airport CTR zones, flying over people). Use a licensed operator.
Over-animation can hurt INP and battery on low-end Android and slow down buyers. The device guard, skip-on-interaction and the single hero sequence rule are mandatory, not optional polish.

Claims must match reality: warranty years, manufacturer warranties (often conditional), supplier logos (only brands actually used and permitted), response times ('odgovor isti dan', '48 h izmjera'), service area. Lightning-protection wiring is licensed electrical work, so only list it if they are licensed.
Content maintenance: if the owner never adds projects, the site goes stale. The CMS must allow phone upload in under 2 minutes per project, or the freelancer should sell a monthly content retainer.

name: PREGIB (The Fold): editorial kinetic direction for Limarija Karamatić
oneLiner: A confident, fashion-magazine kinetic site where everything moves the way sheet metal moves. It is never soft, bouncy or floaty: it is bent, laid and pressed. The flat line of the preloader bends into the red roof peak from the logo. The hero photo is laid in strip by strip like standing-seam panels. The giant headline gets squeezed as if in a press brake. Underneath all of it sits a calm, call-first mobile layer, so a 55-year-old homeowner on a Samsung A-series can still find the phone number in one second. My honest opinion is to build "two sites in one": the Awwwards layer for desktop and for the client's pride, and a fast, plain-spoken phone layer, because that is where 70%+ of the calls will come from.

heroStoryboard.beat: The screen is #0E0F11. A 1px steel-gradient horizontal line (#8A9096 to #C9CDD1 to #8A9096) draws outward from the centre to 60vw. This is a flat sheet seen edge-on. A JetBrains Mono caption sits bottom-left: '0,6 mm · RAL 7016'. Bottom-right shows a real asset-load counter, 000 to 100.

The line bends at two points into a roof peak (Λ), a two-path tween with MorphSVG. It uses a custom 'springback' ease: it overshoots about 3 degrees and settles back, the way real sheet does after an abkant bend. A thin white specular highlight runs along each bend line.

The Λ fills with #D7141A from the apex down (clip-path). The letters of KARAMATIĆ rise from a mask around it (SplitText chars, 25ms stagger), so the red Λ becomes the second A, exactly as in the logo. The masks have 0.2em of top padding so the háček on Ć is not clipped.

The whole preloader plate folds up and away: rotateX 0 to -90deg around its top edge with perspective 1400px. The plate darkens as it turns, like a sheet bent upward in a press. At the same moment the red Λ does a GSAP Flip into the header logo slot (top-left, 28px). Click or any key skips. A sessionStorage flag means it never plays twice in a session. It never runs on touch devices or with reduced motion.

The headline is already painted at its final position: 'POKRIVAMO / ZAGREB.' in Archivo wght 900 / wdth 125, clamp(56px, 15vw, 260px), uppercase, line-height 0.9, bottom-left aligned. This text is the LCP element, so it gets no opacity or clip entrance. Each A is an inline-SVG red triangle with aria-hidden; the real text sits in a visually-hidden span. The top utility row shows the phone number, 'Pon–Sub 7–19' and a WhatsApp icon.

A 3:4 frame in columns 8-12 receives photo 17 (golden-hour tile-profile roof) as 8 vertical 'standing-seam' strips. Each strip drops from translateY(-105%) to 0, left to right, with a 70ms stagger and the springback ease. A 2px #C9CDD1 seam line on each strip edge flashes to 100% on landing, then rests at 15%.
A one-time sun glint (a 20deg diagonal white gradient at 18% opacity, mix-blend: overlay) sweeps across the laid strips: the 'new roof shine'. It is compositor-only (transform: translateX).

The headline's wdth axis settles from 125 to 112, as if pressed into shape. The subline fades up 12px: 'Metalni krovovi, opšavi, oluci i popravci — Zagreb i okolica. Besplatna procjena.' Then the CTAs appear: a solid red [Nazovite 09x xxx xxxx] and an outline [WhatsApp]. Idle state: strips parallax ±4px to the cursor at different depths, so the frame reads as corrugated. The scroll cue is a small tile-profile wave with 'Skrolajte'.

heroStoryboard.t: SCROLL 0-30% of a 150vh pin (desktop, scrub 0.6, Lenis)
heroStoryboard.beat: Opposed drift: line 1 'POKRIVAMO' moves x -12vw and line 2 'ZAGREB.' moves x +8vw. The photo frame's clip-path inset opens from the 3:4 frame (inset 0 0 0 58%) toward full viewport. The strips widen and the seam lines stay visible, so the whole screen becomes a metal roof.

The 8 strips fold up one at a time: rotateX 0 to 90deg, transform-origin at the bottom, staggered across the scrub. Their back faces show #B9BEC2, the grey primer side of real coated sheet. This lifts the 'old roof' to reveal scene 2 underneath: photo 10 (flat roof, trapezoid field, Medvednica on the horizon). A mono caption types in: 'RAVNI KROV · TRAPEZNI LIM + OPŠAV ATIKE · ZAGREB'.

The headline compresses from wdth 112 to 62, the press-brake squeeze, and translates up and shrinks into a header-sized label. Three stat plates slide in from the right with a 90ms stagger: 'XXX+ krovova', 'XX godina iskustva', 'X godina jamstva'. These are real numbers from the client only; never ship placeholders.

The pin releases. The next section (light paper #F2F1EE) rides up over the hero with a tile-profile (crijep-lim) SVG wave as its top edge, overlapping the dark hero the way roof sheets overlap. The motion and the meaning are the same.

heroMobileFallback:
Below 1024px, on touch (pointer: coarse), with reduced motion or on low-end devices (deviceMemory < 4 or hardwareConcurrency <= 4) there is no preloader overlay, no pin, no Lenis, no scrub and no WebGL.

The mobile hero is 100svh and portrait. That suits these photos, because every one was shot vertically on a phone. Photo 17 fills the screen with a bottom-up #0E0F11 gradient behind the text. It lands as 4 strips, not 8, in a pure CSS @keyframes animation (900ms, 60ms stagger, started on first paint, no JS dependency). The glint sweep runs once. The tiny red Λ in the header logo does a 500ms fold as the brand moment, in place of the full preloader.

The headline is 2 lines at clamp(44px, 13vw, 72px), wdth 112, line-height 0.92, and is never animated. It is followed by an 18px subline and two full-width 56px buttons: [Nazovite] (tel:) and [WhatsApp] (wa.me link with a prefilled message 'Pozdrav, trebam procjenu za krov…'). A text link 'Besplatna procjena →' goes to the short form. The phone number is visible without scrolling.

After the hero leaves the viewport, a sticky bottom action bar appears: Nazovi | WhatsApp | Procjena, three equal 56px targets on #1A1D20. The A-triangle glyph stays, since it is just SVG. The section-by-section fold reveals become one-shot IntersectionObserver CSS transitions (opacity plus a 24px rise or a 12deg rotateX). With reduced motion, everything is static and the strips are pre-assembled.
heroTech: Astro page with a single GSAP 3 bundle: core, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, CustomEase, Flip and MorphSVG. All of these plugins have been free since the Webflow acquisition, so there are no licence costs. Conditions are wrapped in gsap.matchMedia() ({isDesktop: '(min-width:1024px) and (pointer:fine)', reduce: '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'}), so everything auto-reverts on resize. **Strips** - 8 absolutely positioned copies of the same (same srcset/sizes, so the browser decodes once), each clipped to its column with clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - (i+1)*12.5%) 0 calc(i*12.5%)). - This keeps object-fit: cover and AVIF srcset working. Slicing with background-position breaks responsive images, so avoid it. - The fold uses a parent with perspective: 1400px. Each strip has transform-style: preserve-3d and a ::after back face in #B9BEC2 with backface-visibility: hidden. **Springback ease** `CustomEase.create('springback','M0,0 C0.55,0 0.62,1.035 0.78,1.03 0.9,1.02 1,1')`. **Headline** - Archivo variable. - `@property --wdth { syntax: ''; inherits: true; initial-value: 125 }` and `font-variation-settings: 'wdth' var(--wdth), 'wght' 900`, tweened by GSAP. - Limit it to the 2-line headline, because animating the width axis re-lays-out text every frame. - Red A triangles are inline SVG inside the text with width: 0.72em, so they scale with the font. **Preloader** - Inline SVG in the HTML: a flat path and a Λ path with matching node counts, MorphSVG between them. - A CSS-only fallback keeps the screen from going blank if JS fails. - Fail-safe: the overlay removes itself after 2.5s no matter what. **Scroll** - Lenis on desktop only (`syncTouch: false`), driven by gsap.ticker: `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. - ScrollTrigger: `pin: true, end: '+=150%', scrub: 0.6, anticipatePin: 1`. - `ScrollTrigger.config({ ignoreMobileResize: true })`. - Call `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` after `document.fonts.ready` and after the hero image decode(). **Glint** A pseudo-element with a linear-gradient, animated with transform only. **Phase 2** (once the timelapse exists) Swap photo 17 for a single 6-8s muted, playsinline, looping

typography:
**Archivo (variable)**
Archivo is on Google Fonts with a wdth 62–125 axis and a wght 100–900 axis. Its latin-ext subset covers U+0100–02BA, which includes Č č Ć ć Ž ž Š š Đ đ; I checked this against the Google Fonts CSS API.
- Display headlines: wght 900, wdth 112–125, uppercase, tracking -0.02em, line-height 0.9 (not tighter, see below), clamp(56px, 15vw, 260px).
- H2: clamp(40px, 7vw, 120px), wght 800, wdth 100–112.
- Body: wght 400, wdth 100. 18/28px on mobile, 19/30px on desktop. Never below 16px, including captions on mobile.
- The width axis is the kinetic device: press-brake squeezes and unfolds.

**Instrument Serif Italic** (Google Fonts, latin-ext)
Use it for at most one accent word or phrase per section, e.g. 'Krov koji *ne pušta*.', 'do *milimetra*'. It gives the fashion-editorial contrast against the heavy grotesk. Size it about 1.1x the surrounding grotesk to match x-heights.

**JetBrains Mono** (Google Fonts, latin-ext)
For spec captions, counters, labels and the phone number in the header. 12–14px, uppercase, tracking +0.08em. Example: '0,6 MM · RAL 7016 · 142 M² · 2025'.

**Self-hosting**
Self-host all fonts with Fontsource or google-webfonts-helper. Do not hotlink Google Fonts: a German court ruled that remote Google Fonts loading leaks IP addresses under GDPR. Keep only the latin and latin-ext subsets, use font-display: swap, and preload only the Archivo woff2 that carries both axes.

**Croatian-specific gotchas**
- Uppercase háčeks and acute accents (Č Ć Š Ž) get clipped by line-height under 0.9 and by SplitText overflow masks. Give masks padding-top 0.2em with an equal negative margin.
- Never let a single 'i' or 'u' end a headline line; join them with a non-breaking space ('u Zagrebu').
- Use the Croatian decimal comma ('0,6 mm') and spaced thousands ('1 200 m²').
- Set hyphenation with lang='hr', and turn hyphens off on display type.
texturesAndMotion:
**Textures** (all cheap, no video backgrounds)
- **Brushed metal:** an SVG feTurbulence with anisotropic baseFrequency='0.002 0.6' (long horizontal streaks). Render it once to a 512px AVIF tile at build time and use it as a 6-10% overlay on Grafit surfaces and as a background-clip: text fill for the ticker and the footer wordmark.
- **Film grain:** a static 256px noise PNG at 3-4% opacity on dark sections only. Never an animated canvas grain on mobile.
- **Standing-seam rhythm:** repeating-linear-gradient hairlines (1px #383E42 every 48px) as faint backgrounds behind section titles.
- **Crijep-lim wave:** an SVG path of the tile-profile silhouette used as section edges and as the scroll-cue icon.
- **Screw-head bullets:** a 6px dot with a 1px ring, like an EPDM washer, as list bullets.
- **Photo grade:** photos get one unified grade and a subtle 2% grain so the phone shots sit together.

**Motion language: 'Lim se savija, ne skakuće'** (metal bends, it does not bounce)
- Only three moves are allowed:
  - **Lay:** vertical drop into place, for strips and cards.
  - **Fold:** rotateX around a horizontal edge with a perspective of 1200-1400px. Back faces are #B9BEC2.
  - **Press:** the variable-font width squeeze.
- No elastic or bubbly easing, no rotateZ spins, no blob morphs, no parallax stacks deeper than two layers.
- **Easing:** a 'springback' CustomEase with a 3% overshoot and a hard settle, used on every landing and fold. Use expo.out for UI and linear for scrubs.
- **Durations:** micro 160-200ms (buttons, cursor), UI 300ms, fold 650-750ms, hero sequence at most 1.3s, page transition 450ms.
- **Staggers:** 50-70ms, always left to right or top to bottom, the order sheets are laid.
- **Scroll:** Lenis on desktop only (lerp 0.1). Native scroll on all touch devices.

**Motion safety**
- prefers-reduced-motion and the in-menu 'Animacije isključene' toggle both switch to opacity-only fades, no pins and no WebGL.
- Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second.
- Every scroll-driven section must make sense as a plain stacked layout first, built that way in the HTML. Animation is a layer added on top.

performancePlan:
**Three tiers, decided before any animation code loads**
- **Full:** min-width 1024px, pointer: fine, no reduced motion, deviceMemory 4 or more and hardwareConcurrency more than 4. Gets the preloader, Lenis, pins, scrub and OGL.
- **Lite:** touch or mid-range. Gets CSS keyframes and IntersectionObserver one-shots, and GSAP core only if needed.
- **Static:** reduced motion, the 'Animacije isključene' toggle, or Save-Data. Gets fades only.

**Budgets**
- Initial JS on mobile under 60KB gzip (the lite tier is mostly CSS).
- Desktop: GSAP and plugins about 70KB, Lenis about 4KB, OGL about 25KB lazy-loaded when the gallery is within 1 viewport.
- CSS under 30KB.
- Fonts: one Archivo woff2 (both axes, latin + latin-ext) about 70-90KB preloaded; Instrument Serif and Mono loaded lazily (font-display: swap).
- Hero image AVIF: about 90-130KB on mobile at 828w and about 250KB on desktop at 1600-2400w, with fetchpriority='high' and loading='eager'. Everything else is lazy, with explicit width and height for CLS 0.

**LCP strategy**
- The LCP element is the headline text, painted immediately at its final position. Only its width axis animates; there is no opacity or clip entrance.
- The strip clones reuse one decoded image.
- The preloader is desktop-only, first visit, 1.5s or less, skippable, and removes itself after 2.5s. Verify with a WebPageTest filmstrip that the content behind it is already painted.

**Avoid**
- No video in the first viewport on mobile. Once the timelapse exists, mobile gets the poster image, and the video starts only on Wi-Fi or a good effective connection type.
- No Google Maps embed (static image plus a link), no chat widgets, no Facebook pixel by default.

**Runtime**
- Animate only transform, opacity and clip-path, plus the width axis on 2 lines of text.
- Use will-change only during active tweens.
- Kill ScrollTriggers via matchMedia on resize. Call ScrollTrigger.refresh() after fonts.ready and after image decode.
- Use svh/dvh units, and set ignoreMobileResize so the iOS address bar does not make pins jump.

**Targets** (field p75)
- LCP under 2.0s on mobile 4G, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.05.
- Lighthouse mobile 90 or above for Performance, 100 for Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO.
- Check monthly in Vercel Speed Insights or CrUX.
risks: Award-site tropes can read as 'an agency showing off' instead of 'a tradesman I trust with my house'. A 55-year-old homeowner may not see where to call. Mitigation: the phone number and WhatsApp are visible in the first mobile viewport, a sticky Nazovi | WhatsApp | Procjena bar, every kinetic headline is followed by a plain-language subline, and phone and WhatsApp clicks are tracked so performance is judged on calls, not on Awwwards.

Scroll-jacking and pinned or horizontal sections feel 'stuck' or broken on Android and confuse older users. Mitigation: no Lenis, no pins and no horizontal hijack on touch. The gallery is a native scroll-snap carousel with a visible next card, arrows and a 'Povucite →' hint. The in-menu 'Animacije isključene' toggle and prefers-reduced-motion are honoured everywhere.

The custom cursor and hover-only reveals do nothing on touch, and a custom cursor can make desktop elderly users lose the pointer. Mitigation: the native cursor is never hidden over fields or buttons, no information is hover-only, and everything has a tap or accordion equivalent.

The source photos are 1200px WhatsApp exports. A full-bleed desktop hero will look soft and undermine the 'ultra premium' promise. Mitigation: get the originals from the client's phones now and schedule the timelapse and drone shoot. Until then, keep large images in 3:4 frames rather than full-bleed, with grain, and upscale only the hero if necessary.

Animating the variable-font width axis and SplitText masks can clip Croatian diacritics (Č Ć Š Ž) and cause layout jank. Mitigation: line-height 0.9 or more, mask padding, width-axis animation limited to the 2-line headline, and tests with real Croatian copy (not lorem ipsum).

The glossy AI-rendered raster logo clashes with a flat editorial system and blurs at small sizes. The client may be attached to it. Mitigation: present the flat vector redraw as 'the same logo, made for screens', and keep the glossy version for the van and social media.

Real trust content is missing: years in business, number of roofs, warranty terms, Google reviews, OIB, before/after shots. Kinetic counters with invented numbers would be dishonest and legally risky. Mitigation: a content checklist signed off before build. Sections stay hidden until their data exists.

GSAP + Lenis + View Transitions integration bugs (stale ScrollTrigger positions after fonts or images load, iOS Safari address-bar resize, back-button scroll restoration). Mitigation: a multi-page app (no SPA router), refresh hooks, and testing on a real iPhone and Samsung early, not in the last week.

Scope creep. WebGL, the preloader, the loupe and the fold transitions are each a day or more. Mitigation: a pre-agreed cut list. If the schedule slips, drop OGL first (use a CSS hover zoom), then the loupe, then the preloader. The panel-lay hero and the mobile layer are non-negotiable.
Maintenance: the client cannot safely edit the animated layouts. Mitigation: Keystatic edits only projects, reviews, FAQ and contact data. Layouts are code.

GDPR and compliance: remote Google Fonts, map embeds, form data with photos. Mitigation: self-hosted fonts, a static map, cookieless analytics, a privacy page, and form data retention stated. WCAG 2.2 AA as the standard even though a microenterprise is likely exempt from the European Accessibility Act.
